newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia sells HRK143 mln 42-day bills, rate falls.
newsitem.headline: Croatia sells HRK143 mln 42-day bills, rate falls.

text.p: Croatia's Finance Ministry said it raised 143 million kuna in 42-day treasury bills at an auction on Tuesday.
The issued amount fell short of the 150 million kuna target although bids overshot it by 12 million, it said in a news release.
The new 42-day issue was priced higher at 98.946 percent, compared to 98.919 two weeks ago, and interest fell 24 basis points to 9.26 percent. Full results are on Reuters page MFHT.
A lion's share of 82.46 percent went to banking investors. Foreigners cannot participate at the auctions directly but they can place their bids through Croatian banks.
The ministry said it had a round sum of 500 million kuna in outstanding 42-, 91- and 182-day T-bills.
It set the next auction for June 10, when another 50 million kuna in 91-day T-bills will be offered to investors.
